(2) When 𝔠_0 ≠ 1, the character factor is sgn(N a)ψ^{-1}(a𝔟_𝒜^{-1}), not ψ(𝔟_𝒜). Under the convention of Remark 8.5 the two agree when 𝔠_0 = 1. Check of (1) at the cusp ∞. findings.claim: The proof of Theorem B.8, which is the paper's proof of Kurihara's conjecture (Theorem 1.4), contains a false step. Item 323 copies it as if it were correct, and no sourceIssue records it. After Lemma B.6 is applied to H' = H^{Σ∖Σ_0}, the paper says that multiplying by ∏_{v∈Σ∖Σ_0} N I_v gives 'exactly the terms in (178)', and from this it deduces (179). (The extraction numbers these equations (182) and (183).) The step fails. In Lemma B.6 applied to H', each factor N I_v with v ∈ Σ̄∖J_0 is the norm of the inertia group of H'/F, that is, of the image Ī_v of I_v in G' = G/K, where K = I_{Σ∖Σ_0}. In (178) the factor is N_G I_v. The product P = ∏_{u∈Σ∖Σ_0} N_G I_u kills the kernel of ℤ[G] → ℤ[G/K]. Also N_G I_v maps to #(I_v ∩ K)·N_{G'} Ī_v. So each term of (178) is the corresponding multiplied term times the integer ∏_{v∈Σ̄∖J_0} #(I_v ∩ K). When p divides this integer, (179) is false. The last sentence of the proof ('Writing J = Σ_0 ∪ J_0, we obtain the expression (176)') makes the same identification in reverse. The two errors cancel in the printed formula, but the argument does not prove (176) in this case. Counterexample to (179) over F = ℚ: let p be an odd prime, ℓ ≡ 1 (mod p) a prime, K the cyclic degree-p field cut out by ψ_1ψ_2 (ψ_1 of conductor p² and order p, ψ_2 of conductor ℓ and order p), k = ℚ(√−q) with q ≡ 3 (mod 4) prime such that p and ℓ split in k, and H = Kk. Then G = C × ⟨c⟩ with #C = p, I_p = I_ℓ = C, I_q = ⟨c⟩, Σ = S_∞ ∪ {p} and Σ̄ = {ℓ, q}. Take Σ_0 = S_∞ and J_0 = {q}. The (178) term is N_C·N_C·F = p·N_C·F, where (F) = Fitt(∇^T_{S_∞∪{q}}(k)_p^-) ≠ 0 because this minus module is finite. The multiplied term is N_C·F, since ℓ is unramified in k. On the minus side, every generator of the left side (177) maps into p²F·ℤ_p under ℤ_p[G]^- → ℤ_p[G/C]^- ≅ ℤ_p. The generators with p or ℓ in J vanish there because p and ℓ split in k, which makes the corresponding α-columns zero modulo C by Lemma B.3. But N_C·F maps to pF. So the right side of (179) is strictly larger than its left side. The stated formula (176) is not shown to be false: in this example it agrees with (177) once Theorem 3.7 is used. What fails is the proof.

findings.claim: Lemma 4.1 replaces Σ' by Σ'' = Σ' − {v ∈ T : v | p}, and from then on (§§5–9 and Appendix A) the paper works with a T that contains no primes above p. But Σ'' need not satisfy condition (1), which the paper assumes wherever these sets are used afterwards: the definition and Lemma 3.1 of the Selmer module (§3.1), Lemma 2.1 (applied inside Lemma 5.3), the uniqueness of minus-part generators in the proof of Lemma 5.5, §6 and Appendix A (Lemma A.4 uses that O^*_{H,Σ,Σ'} is Z-torsion free). Example: F = Q, H = Q(i), p = 3, T = {3}. T is unramified in H and satisfies (1), because no root of unity of Q(i) other than 1 is ≡ 1 mod 3. Then Σ' = {2, 3} and Σ'' = {2}, and Σ'' fails (1) because −1 ≡ i ≡ 1 mod (1+i). Correspondingly Θ_{S_∞,{2}} = 1/2 ∉ Z[G]: its value at the trivial character is ζ(0)(1 − 2) = 1/2 and its value at χ_{−4} is L(χ_{−4},0) = 1/2. Lemma 2.1's claim L_{S_∞,T}(H/H^+,ε,0) ∈ Z also fails for T = {2}, where the value is 1/2. So the reduction does not deliver the hypotheses under which §§5–6 and the appendix are stated. The extraction records no sourceIssue for this. Its items 92 and 93 require 'T satisfying the Deligne–Ribet condition (1)', and item 89 requires that T contain no primes above p. Lemma 4.1 does not give both at once, so the chain from item 36 through Lemma 4.1 (items 84, 85) to Theorem 5.1 (item 93) does not compose as written. The gap can be repaired. Σ'' does satisfy the p-part of (1): no nontrivial root of unity of p-power order in H is ≡ 1 modulo every prime above Σ''. The reason is that a root of unity of p-power order is ≡ 1 modulo every prime above p, so the p-adic primes of T never contribute to (1) at p. Each later use of (1) only involves torsion of order prime to p once tensored with Z_p; for example, the w_T of the smoothed class number formula becomes prime to p. Severity set to medium by the coordinator: every later use of condition (1) is made after tensoring with Z_p, where its p-part suffices and Σ'' satisfies it; the statements of items 92 and 93 remain true, and only their hypotheses must be weakened so that the chain from Lemma 4.1 composes.

findings.claim: Lemma 5.4 (Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H)_ψ ≅ Sel_Σ^{Σ'}(H_ψ)_ψ) has its proof omitted as 'nearly identical to Lemma 4.2', but the key step of Lemma 4.2 does not carry over. Lemma 4.2's middle vertical arrow is 'clearly an isomorphism (Galois theory)'. That rests on [H:H_χ] being prime to p: the R-component is then an eigenspace for the prime-to-p group G', so (Hom(U,Z) ⊗ O)_R = Hom_O((U ⊗ O)^{G'=χ}, O). For (H_ψ, O_ψ) the situation is different. Because χ is faithful on G', K = ker ψ lies in G_p, so [H : H_ψ] is a power of p. Write U = O^*_{H,S',Σ'}. The corresponding middle map is Hom(U,Z)_K ⊗ O_ψ → Hom(U^K,Z) ⊗ O_ψ. Before the tensor product, the map Hom(U,Z)_K → Hom(U^K,Z) is surjective, and its kernel is the torsion subgroup Ĥ^{-1}(K, Hom(U,Z)) of the coinvariants. This group is nonzero for general lattices: for K = Z/p acting on Z[ζ_p] through ζ_p, Ĥ^{-1} = Z/p. The paper gives no argument that this kernel, or its image in Sel(H)_ψ, vanishes for the unit lattice. The diagram of Lemma 4.2 therefore yields only a surjection Sel(H)_ψ ↠ Sel(H_ψ)_ψ. That surjection gives Fitt_O(Sel(H)_ψ) ⊂ Fitt_O(Sel(H_ψ)_ψ), which is the wrong direction for (68), so the isomorphism is genuinely needed. The statement is consistent with Theorem 3.3 when L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ,0) ≠ 0: both modules then have Fitting ideal (L_{Σ,Σ'}(ψ,0)), and a surjection between finite O-modules of equal size is an isomorphism. That consistency cannot be used inside the proof of Theorem 3.3, so the step is a gap, not an error. Item 102 says only 'The proof is that of Lemma 4.2 ... with (H_χ, R) replaced by (H_ψ, O_ψ)', which hides the gap.

findings.claim: No item covers how complex-analytic Hilbert modular forms become forms with coefficients in Z, O or Frac O. The paper defines M_k(𝔫,A) := M_k(𝔫,Z) ⊗ A. It then places complex forms in these spaces: E_k(ψ_S,1) ∈ M_k(𝔫, Frac O, ψ) in §7.3, the specialisations ψ(f) ∈ M_k(𝔫,O,ψ), and the newforms f ∈ M, whose stabilised coefficients c(𝔞,f_p) are assumed to lie in O. Each placement needs Shimura's rationality theorem: M_k(𝔫) has a basis of forms with rational q-expansion, so M_k(𝔫,K) = M_k(𝔫,Q) ⊗ K for subfields K ⊂ C. Each also needs bounded denominators, M_k(𝔫,Q) = M_k(𝔫,Z) ⊗ Q, together with a fixed embedding of Q̄ into the p-adic coefficient field. The extraction treats M_k(𝔫,Z) purely as a definition. The authors had cited Shimura's Annals 1975 paper, Theorem 7, for exactly this, but in the TeX source that paragraph ('Forms over a ring R') sits inside a comment environment. The reference survives as [43] in the printed bibliography and is cited nowhere in the printed text.

The second criterion is false without that hypothesis. In the paper the hypothesis is implicit, since T is disjoint from S ⊇ S_ram. Counterexample: F = ℚ, H = ℚ(ζ_5), T = {5}. Then ζ_5 ≡ 1 modulo the unique prime (1 − ζ_5) above 5, so condition (1) fails although 5 > [ℚ:ℚ] + 1 = 2. findings.claim: Item 322's proof sketch says that Theorem 3.7 is applied to H^{Σ∖Σ_0}/F, 'whose Σ-set is Σ_0'. This is false in general. If some v ∈ Σ_0∖S_∞ has I_v ⊂ I_{Σ∖Σ_0}, for example two primes above p with the same inertia group, then v is unramified in H^{Σ∖Σ_0}. The Σ-set of that field, S_∞ together with its ramified primes above p, is then strictly smaller than Σ_0, and Theorem 3.7 for that field computes the Fitting ideal of Sel with a smaller depletion set. To reach Sel^T_{Σ_0}, one first adds the unramified places Σ_0∖Σ(H^{Σ∖Σ_0}) to the depletion set at the level of the quadratically presented keystone module (Lemma 4.3), and then repeats the argument of Theorem 3.7. The paper's 'follows directly from Theorem 3.7' leaves out this step. The step is easy, so this is a small gap that does not affect the result.
findings.evidence: The paper (arXiv v3, pp. 95–96), proof of Lemma B.7: 'By the same argument as in (171), we have Fitt^{s−s_0}_{R_0^-} ∇^T_{Σ_0}(H^{Σ∖Σ_0})^-_p = (Fitt_{R_0^-} Sel^T_{Σ_0}(H^{Σ∖Σ_0})^-_p)^#. The result then follows directly from Theorem 3.7.' Theorem 3.7 (p. 22, TeX label t:ks) concerns Sel^T_Σ(H) for Σ = S_∞ ∪ {v ∈ S_ram : v | p} of the field in question. Lemma 4.3 (TeX label l:selchi) adds unramified primes to the depletion set when the smaller Selmer module is quadratically presented.

findings.where: PAPER-DASGUPTA-KAKDE-23/259, /278, /301 (local reciprocity map and its normalisation)
findings.claim: No item covers the local Artin map rec : F_𝔭^* → G_𝔭^{ab}, which the paper uses to define the unramified character η_𝔭 in (110) and (114) and to choose the elements σ_i in the proof of Theorem 9.10. Its normalisation matters. The paper uses the convention in which rec(ϖ^{-1}) lifts the arithmetic Frobenius, so a uniformiser goes to the inverse Frobenius. This is the opposite of the convention pinned by the Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory roadmap, in which a uniformiser goes to arithmetic Frobenius. The identity c_i = (A_i/C_i)(U_{𝔭_i} − ψ(𝔭_i) + I) in the proof of Theorem 9.10 holds with the paper's convention: η_𝔭(σ_i) = U_{𝔭_i}^{-1} and ψ(σ_i) = ψ(𝔭_i)^{-1}. With the other convention it becomes an identity involving U^{-1} and fails as written. A formaliser who takes rec from the planned layer would get the sign wrong.
findings.evidence: The paper (arXiv v3, p. 66): 'η_𝔭(rec(ϖ^{-1})) = c(𝔭, f_p) … We adopt Serre's conventions [42] for the reciprocity map. Therefore rec(ϖ^{-1}) is a lifting to G_𝔭^{ab} of the Frobenius element on the maximal unramified extension of F_𝔭'. p. 76: 'choose an element σ_i ∈ G_{𝔭_i} ⊂ G_F that lifts rec(ϖ_i) … c_i = b(σ_i)ψ(𝔭_i)ε^{1−k}_cyc(σ_i) = (A_i/C_i)(U_{𝔭_i} − ψ(𝔭_i) + I)'. The Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory roadmap text in the atlas, §2.6 'Frobenius convention', reads: 'All local and global Artin maps use arithmetic Frobenius. For an unramified extension of nonarchimedean local fields, a uniformizer maps to the automorphism inducing x ↦ x^q on the residue field'. A search of item names and statements for local reciprocity, uniformiser normalisation or arithmetic/geometric Frobenius finds no such item; the convention appears only inside items 258, 259 and 301.
findings.fix: Add a definition item 'Local Artin map rec : F_𝔭^* → G_𝔭^{ab} in the paper's normalisation (rec(ϖ^{-1}) restricts to arithmetic Frobenius on F_𝔭^{nr})', locator §9.1, p. 66.
